title: Fast dynamic vertex colouring against adaptive updates
formal: Can a Las Vegas randomized fully dynamic structure maintain a proper (Δ+1)-coloring against adaptive updates in expected amortized polylogarithmic time with constant-time color queries?
definitions:
Fix n≥1 and a supplied bound 0≤Δ≤n−1. Start from the empty simple graph on [n]; insertions and deletions of edges are promised always to keep maximum degree at most Δ. Maintain a single coloring χ:[n]→{1,…,Δ+1} valid at the end of each update, with χ(u)≠χ(v) on every current edge. A query for v returns its current χ(v), consistently between updates. Recoloring any number of vertices is allowed but all work to change their stored colors counts. Use a uniform word-RAM with Θ(log(n+2))-bit words, O((n+m)log^c(n+2)) space and O(n log^c(n+2)) initialization.

The adversary sees all earlier query answers and public updates and may choose the next operation from them, including querying every vertex. It does not see private random coins or internal memory. For every such strategy and every finite operation horizon, outputs must be correct with probability one and expected total time must be at most initialization plus O(U log^c(n+2)+Q), where U,Q are the numbers of updates and queries. Every color query has O(1) worst-case time. The constant c and hidden constants are independent of Δ. The adversary is not required to fix the update sequence in advance.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked algorithm and proof of all stated guarantees, or prove the precise target impossible. State any complexity hypothesis used in a conditional impossibility.
context: The adaptive-adversary paper separates this model from the faster guarantees available against oblivious updates.
why: Adaptive robustness is a central obstacle to making very fast randomized dynamic colorings reliable in interactive use.

sentences: The palette has one more color than a fixed promised maximum degree.
Colors must stay proper after every edge update.
An adversary can choose future updates after inspecting past color answers.
Random coins and internal memory stay private.
The target combines always-correct coloring with polylogarithmic expected update work.
